items.title: HR Business Partner
items.description: About this Team The HR Business Partner (HRBP) team at OpenAI partners with leaders to navigate complex organizational and talent decisions where the right path is not always obvious. We are building a higher-leverage HRBP model: staying close enough to the business to understand its realities, while focusing our time on the work that requires judgment, influence, context, and leadership partnership. This role is for an HRBP who can diagnose ambiguous situations, translate business strategy into organizational and talent decisions, coach leaders through consequential choices, and help build the operating rhythms that enable scale. While the role spans both strategic and operational work, the bar is not to be helpful on everything. The bar is to improve decision quality, strengthen leadership capability, and increase organizational effectiveness. We operate with urgency, empathy, and sound judgment. We value sincerity, intellectual honesty, and collaboration over ego, and focus relentlessly on creating meaningful impact. About this Role This role is part of a shared hiring pathway for HRBPs at OpenAI. Instead of hiring directly for a single team, we evaluate candidates holistically first, then identify the best fit across our organization as you advance. This approach ensures alignment between your skills, interests, and where our needs are greatest—whether that’s partnering with technical leaders in engineering, supporting product teams driving user impact, or enabling operational excellence across business functions. As a Senior HR Business Partner, you’ll be a trusted advisor to leaders and their teams. You’ll help set direction for how we organize, grow, and lead—stepping in as both a sounding board and a problem-solver. This role mixes strategic advising with hands-on support: you’ll design better systems, coach managers through complex situations, and help us make trade-offs that keep our people and mission in balance. This is an individual contributor role reporting to an HRBP Lead. In this role, you will: - Shape high-performing, resilient teams: Partner with leaders to design structures, talent plans, and ways of working that enable strong performance and sustainable growth. - Collaborate for a seamless experience: Partner with fellow HRBPs, COEs, and cross-functional leaders to build an employee experience rooted in humanity, humility, and impact. - Evolve People programs: Strengthen performance, engagement, and retention processes—building solutions that are lightweight, scalable, and aligned with how OpenAI operates. - Guide and develop managers: Offer candid, actionable feedback and help managers build leadership muscle across their teams. - Anticipate and act fast: Stay close to the business to identify challenges early, diagnose root causes, and deliver lasting solutions that adapt as priorities shift. - Lead change that matters: Drive organizational changes with empathy, clarity, and rigor—finding creative paths forward when playbooks don’t exist. You might thrive in this role if you have: - Deep HRBP expertise: 7–10+ years of HR experience, including at least 5 years as an HR Business Partner in high-growth or complex environments. - Strategic partnering: Able to see the big picture, guide leaders through tough trade-offs, and adapt quickly when priorities shift. - Multipliers who create impact: Skilled at giving candid feedback with care and building leadership capabilities across organizations. - Scrappy problem solving: Uses sound judgment to diagnose challenges, test creative solutions, and chart a path forward without a playbook. - Change leadership with calm & clarity: Brings steadiness, empathy, and influence in moments of ambiguity or transition. - High integrity: Known for discretion, fairness, and trustworthiness when the stakes are high. Workplace & Location This role is based in our San Francisco or New York office, and we aren’t considering remote applications at this time. We do encourage you to apply even if you prefer a fully remote role as location factors may change over time. We offer relocation support to new employees, and we use a hybrid model: three days in the office per week with optional work from home on Thursdays and Fridays. About OpenAI OpenAI is an AI research and deployment company dedicated to ensuring that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products. AI is an extremely powerful tool that must be created with safety and human needs at its core, and to achieve our mission, we must encompass and value the many different perspectives, voices, and experiences that form the full spectrum of humanity. We are an equal opportunity employer, and we do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, age, veteran status, disability, genetic information, or other applicable legally protected characteristic. For additional information, please see OpenAI’s Affirmative Action and Equal Employment Opportunity Policy Statement https://cdn.openai.com/policies/eeo-policy-statement.pdf. Background checks for applicants will be administered in accordance with applicable law, and qualified applicants with arrest or conviction records will be considered for employment consistent with those laws, including the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act, for US-based candidates. In addition, job duties require access to secure and protected information technology systems and related data security obligations. items.title: Data Program Manager, Science
items.description: About the Team OpenAI’s Research Data team exists to accelerate the evaluation, safety and capabilities of our models and products. Made up of technical operators and software engineers, we design the methods through which we acquire and create data. About the Role As a Data Program Manager, Science, you will help researchers develop and execute scientific data programs, connecting OpenAI’s research priorities with relevant data, expertise and external partners. You’ll work closely with researchers to understand their needs, assess the scientific and practical value of opportunities, and develop partnerships across the scientific ecosystem. The work could range from acquiring existing datasets to shaping research collaborations. You’ll carry opportunities from initial investigation through commercial discussions, agreements, delivery and research use, exercising sound judgement around sensitive data and relationships. Our current work focuses particularly on biology and chemistry. We welcome different combinations of scientific, technical and partnership experience. This role is based in our San Francisco HQ. In this role, you will: - Develop data strategies with Research. Translate research goals, model limitations and evaluation gaps into evidence needs and success criteria. Compare acquisition with internal, public and commissioned alternatives. - Find distinctive sources for research. Build trusted local and international relationships across research and industry, including organisations at the scientific frontier. - Assess opportunities in scientific context. Inspect samples for provenance, context, quality and completeness. Assess usefulness, involving researchers and specialists as needed. - Shape partnerships with lasting scientific value. Understand partners’ ambitions and define pilots, deliverables and acceptance criteria, considering expertise, scientific contribution and continuing relationships alongside commercial terms. - Lead commercial and operational execution. Develop proposals, assess pricing and negotiate terms. Coordinate Legal, Privacy, Security, Procurement and engineering to clarify permissions, responsibilities and delivery. - Navigate sensitive collaborations. Understand institutional interests and confidentiality. Identify ethical, privacy, security and misuse concerns early, involving specialists to develop responsible arrangements. - Follow through into research use. Coordinate preparation, ingestion, access and documentation. Gather researcher feedback to inform whether to expand, change or stop. - Make thoughtful portfolio decisions. Recommend options based on research value, cost, timing and capacity. Identify shared needs and opportunities for useful collaboration across projects. - Make the work more repeatable. Use code, APIs, automation and AI tools to improve sourcing, assessment and delivery. Resolve recurring blockers with engineers and retain partner knowledge and research feedback. You might thrive in this role if you: - Have substantial grounding in biology, chemistry or related sciences through research, industry or equivalent experience, and engage critically with methods and evidence. - Have delivered complex scientific, data or partnership projects, with depth in one or more of scientific data and evaluation, commercial partnerships or research collaborations across organisations. - Exercise sound judgement: test claims, match evidence to research needs and make clear recommendations while acknowledging uncertainty. - Work directly with data: inspect unfamiliar files, investigate quality and use Python, SQL, APIs and AI-assisted coding to answer questions and reduce manual work. - Build trust through careful listening, precise questions and thoughtful negotiation. You bring relevant local and international relationships, or a demonstrated ability to develop them, and understand what partners value beyond the transaction. - Exercise discretion, recognising the limits of your expertise and authority and when scientific, ethical or safety questions need specialist input. - Thrive in a fast-moving environment, taking broad ownership across multiple projects and moving readily between scientific, technical and commercial questions. You prioritise thoughtfully as needs change, making clear decisions about where to focus and what can wait. - Enjoy getting your hands dirty, bringing energy and creative problem solving to unfamiliar or ambiguous opportunities. You turn them into practical plans and follow through on the details. - Learn exceptionally quickly, developing your understanding of AI training, evaluation and unfamiliar research areas to become a useful collaborator. - We welcome different combinations of scientific, technical and partnership experience. You do not need equal depth in every area. About OpenAI OpenAI is an AI research and deployment company dedicated to ensuring that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. items.title: Customer Advocacy Manager
items.description: About Glean: Glean is the Work AI platform that helps everyone work smarter with AI. What began as the industry’s most advanced enterprise search has evolved into a full-scale Work AI ecosystem, powering intelligent Search, an AI Assistant, and scalable AI agents on one secure, open platform. With over 100 enterprise SaaS connectors, flexible LLM choice, and robust APIs, Glean gives organizations the infrastructure to govern, scale, and customize AI across their entire business - without vendor lock-in or costly implementation cycles. At its core, Glean is redefining how enterprises find, use, and act on knowledge. Its Enterprise Graph and Personal Knowledge Graph map the relationships between people, content, and activity, delivering deeply personalized, context-aware responses for every employee. This foundation powers Glean’s agentic capabilities - AI agents that automate real work across teams by accessing the industry’s broadest range of data: enterprise and world, structured and unstructured, historical and real-time. The result: measurable business impact through faster onboarding, hours of productivity gained each week, and smarter, safer decisions at every level. Recognized by Fast Company as one of the World’s Most Innovative Companies (Top 10, 2025), by CNBC’s Disruptor 50, Bloomberg’s AI Startups to Watch (2026), Forbes AI 50, and Gartner’s Tech Innovators in Agentic AI, Glean continues to accelerate its global impact. With customers across 50+ industries and 1,000+ employees in more than 25 countries, we’re helping the world’s largest organizations make every employee AI-fluent, and turning the superintelligent enterprise from concept into reality. If you’re excited to shape how the world works, you’ll help build systems used daily across Microsoft Teams, Zoom, ServiceNow, Zendesk, GitHub, and many more. You'll be deeply embedded where people get things done. You'll ship agentic capabilities on an open, extensible stack, with the craft and care required for enterprise trust, as we bring Work AI to every employee, in every company. About the Role: Glean is seeking a Customer Advocacy Manager to join our Marketing Team and help build a world-class customer advocacy engine. As a Customer Advocacy Manager, you’ll partner closely with Sales, Customer Success, Product Marketing, and Comms/PR to support our reference request desk, support the production of compelling customer stories, coordinate speakers for events, and drive reviews and social proof— turning customer proof into stories that move markets and bringing measurable outcomes to life. You will: Reference Desk Support intake, qualification, and fulfillment of sales and marketing reference requests; uphold SLAs and provide clear status updates to stakeholders. Maintain accurate referenceability, approvals, and logo rights; coordinate with customer Comms/PR and Legal to ensure compliance. Storytelling and content production Assist in sourcing, scoping, and delivering customer stories across formats: written case studies , customer films , fireside chats , blog quotes, and social snippets Coordinate interviews, compile notes, draft briefs, manage reviews/approvals, and track status through publication and enablement hand‑off. Coordinate with creative vendors and internal teams on video shoots and design deliverables (briefs, schedules, releases). Events, Reviews, and Social Proof Recruit and prep customer speakers for Glean events (ie. Glean:LIVE ), webinars, and executive programs (ie. Customer Advisory Days ). Plan and execute peer-review campaigns across platforms, channels, and events while avoiding overlapping asks and protecting the customer relationship. Develop customer awards and recognition programs, including nominations, selection criteria, approvals, vendor and budget coordination, gifting, and related storytelling. Support event activations that recruit advocates and gather approved proof, then extend existing advocacy into new opportunities and reusable assets. Programmization Maintain systems of record for reference requests, customer touchpoints, stories, speakers, champions, reviews, logos, and permissions; create workflows, templates, playbooks, governance, and automation that improve efficiency and experience. About you: Basic Qualifications 4+ years in customer marketing, customer reference programs, product marketing, PR/comms, or customer success in B2B SaaS. Excellent project coordination, organization, and attention to detail across multi‑stakeholder projects. Strong interviewing and writing skills; able to turn raw inputs into clear, outcome‑driven narratives. Strong executive presence Confident, concise communicator with internal and customer stakeholders. Tool fluency: Google Workspace; Salesforce ; project tools (e.g., Asana ); comfort with spreadsheets and light data hygiene. Preferred Qualifications Experience running a customer reference desk or champion community and coordinating speakers, executive programs, webinars, conferences, or multi-city events. Experience producing case studies, customer videos, social content, or review campaigns and working with creative or event vendors, rewards, gifting, budgets, permissions, releases, logo rights, and communications or legal approvals. Experience with program analytics, CRM reporting, marketing attribution, workflow automation, or AI-powered tools, plus familiarity with enterprise AI, AI agents, and related technical and business use cases. Location: This role is 4 days a week our of one of our Bay Area offices (Mountain View or San Francisco) Compensation: The standard base salary range for this position is $139,000 - $149,000 annually. Compensation offered will be determined by factors such as location, level, job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. Certain roles may be eligible for variable compensation, equity, and benefits. We offer a comprehensive benefits package including competitive compensation, Medical, Vision, and Dental coverage, generous time-off policy, and the opportunity to contribute to your 401k plan to support your long-term goals. When you join, you'll receive a home office improvement stipend, as well as an annual education and wellness stipends to support your growth and wellbeing. We foster a vibrant company culture through regular events, and provide healthy lunches daily to keep you fueled and focused. We are a diverse bunch of people and we want to continue to attract and retain a diverse range of people into our organization. We're committed to an inclusive and diverse company. We do not discriminate based on gender, ethnicity, sexual orientation, religion, civil or family status, age, disability, or race. #LI-HYBRID AI-First Mindset at Glean: At Glean, AI fluency is core to how we work and we're committed to ensuring every new hire feels confident integrating AI into their everyday work. As part of the interview process, you'll complete a brief AI-focused exercise or discussion so we can understand how you think about, design, and use AI to drive impact in your role. Feel free to reference any tools, platforms, or workflows you use today — prior Glean experience isn't required. Global Data Privacy Notice for Job Candidates and Applicants: Depending on your location, the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA), or other privacy laws may regulate the way we manage the data of job applicants. Our full notice outlining how data will be processed as part of the application procedure for applicable locations is available in our Privacy Policy . By submitting your application, you are agreeing to our use and processing of your data as required. US applicants and their applications are subject to arbitration of disputes as outlined in our Applicant Arbitration Agreement . By clicking “Submit Application,” I confirm that I have read the Global Data Privacy Notice and the Applicant Arbitration Agreement , and I agree to the terms.

items.title: Software Engineer II - Rust - Pro
items.location_text: Brazil, Peru, Sweden, Colombia, Argentina, Romania, Cyprus, Slovenia, Lithuania, South Africa, Czech Republic, Hungary, Mexico, Chile, Poland, Slovakia, Bulgaria
items.description: BUILDING THE FUTURE OF OPEN FINANCE Payward - the parent company behind Kraken, NinjaTrader, Breakout, xStocks, Payward Services and CF Benchmarks - has spent the last 15 years building one of the most modern and globally accessible financial infrastructure platforms in the industry, built to advance an open, global financial system. The team Founded in 2011, Kraken is one of the world’s longest-standing crypto platforms, trusted by over 10 million individuals and institutions across the globe. It offers spot trading, margin, futures, staking, and OTC services, with products built for both individual investors and institutional clients. The Pro team is responsible for everything to do with the trading backend services such as the matching engine, market data gateways, internal and external APIs, and various other trading services. The team is located globally and responsibilities are split into sub-teams, working with various tech stacks. Our teams code in Rust and C++ and work agile around the globe. The Opportunity - Design and implement robust Rust and C++ services and libraries that power trading, payments, and crypto experiences with a focus on reliability, performance, and user impact. - Write reusable, testable, and highly efficient code that scales across teams and supports revenue-critical systems without compromising safety or security. - Collaborate on large-scale distributed systems architecture, translating evolving product requirements into resilient, low-latency solutions. - Work alongside hundreds of experienced Rust and C++ engineers, contributing to a high-performance, product-driven engineering culture. What You Bring - 3+ years of software engineering experience - Experience building financial trading focused products - Proficient in writing network services or asynchronous code in Rust - Experience with modern C++, including performance-sensitive, low-latency systems - Have a security-first mindset during system design to ensure robustness - Demonstrate the ability to autonomously debug issues across the stack (OS, network, application) - Apply a solid understanding of distributed systems and technologies, including RPC protocols, Kafka, and Event-Driven Systems, to design scalable solutions - Collaborate effectively with product teams to gather requirements and constraints for designing appropriate systems - Take complete end-to-end ownership of systems and libraries Unless a specific application deadline is stated in the job posting, applications are accepted on an ongoing basis. Please note, applicants are permitted to redact or remove information on their resume that identifies age, date of birth, or dates of attendance at or graduation from an educational institution. We consider qualified applicants with criminal histories for employment on our team, assessing candidates in a manner consistent with the requirements of the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance. OUR COMMITMENT Payward is powered by people from around the world and we celebrate the diverse talents, backgrounds, contributions, and unique perspectives that everyone brings to the table. We hire based on merit, seeking out people with the right abilities, knowledge, and skills for the job. We encourage you to apply for roles where you don't fully meet the listed requirements, especially if you're passionate or knowledgeable about crypto. We may ask candidates to complete job-related skills or work-style assessments as part of our hiring process. These assessments evaluate competencies relevant to the role and are applied consistently across candidates for similar positions. Results are considered alongside experience and interviews, and are not the sole basis for any employment decision. As an equal opportunity employer, we don't tolerate discrimination or harassment of any kind, whether based on race, ethnicity, age, gender identity, citizenship, religion, sexual orientation, disability, pregnancy, veteran status, or any other protected characteristic as outlined by federal, state, or local laws. Stay connected Follow us on Twitter https://twitter.com/krakenfx Learn on the Kraken Blog https://blog.kraken.com/#:~:text=Enter%20your%20email%20address Connect on LinkedIn https://www.linkedin.com/company/kraken-exchange/ Candidate Privacy Notice https://www.kraken.com/legal/candidate-privacy-notice

items.title: Partner Marketing Lead, Resellers
items.location_text: San Francisco, CA | New York City, NY
items.description: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the role Anthropic's Claude Partner Network (CPN) Reseller track lets authorized partners sell Claude directly to end customers. These partners bring Claude into accounts that Anthropic can't reach alone, and they need marketing that helps them build a real Claude practice: campaigns they can run with their own teams, funding they can put to work, and proof that moves them up through the partner tiers. This is a foundational, first-in-seat role with wide scope. You'll be the first dedicated partner marketer for the reseller track, and you'll lead it globally. You'll set its marketing strategy, define the standards and playbooks partners run against, and build the tier-advancement path from the ground up. You'll work across regions and with a network of agency partners to deliver programs at global scale. You'll shape how reseller marketing fits into Anthropic's broader partner strategy, working with Partnerships, Commercial Operations, Channel Account Managers, Partner Operations, Customer Marketing, and Communications to make sure reseller activity and Anthropic's direct sales point in the same direction. You'll also set the bar for the marketers who join the practice as it grows. Key responsibilities Set the marketing strategy for the reseller track, including priorities, investment choices, and quarterly and annual plans that connect partner activity to registered pipeline and reseller revenue Define the reseller marketing playbook and co-marketing standards, and keep them current as the program launches and expands Represent the partner marketing perspective in program design, working with Partnerships, Commercial Operations, and Legal on how benefits, MDF, and tier criteria will work in practice Build joint marketing plan templates for reseller partners, including campaign calendars and success metrics Source, select, and manage the agency partners that support reseller programs globally, including scope, budgets, quality standards, and performance reviews, and build a regional roster that can scale as the program expands Run partner-led campaigns with those agencies, using co-branded and localized kits for each market, and help partners adapt them for their own buyers Own partner marketing funds (MDF) end to end: help partners build proposals, track approvals and documentation, and connect every funded activity to registered pipeline Help partners reach their next tier by planning the customer stories, certification pushes, and public proof points each tier requires, on a timeline that fits the January and July tier reviews Turn partner wins into customer stories with Customer Marketing, from interview through partner and Anthropic approvals Coordinate joint announcements and press with Anthropic Communications, managing review timelines and holding partner copy to Anthropic's messaging and brand standards Partner with Channel Account Managers and the field on audience and account targeting, so reseller campaigns extend Anthropic’s reach into new customers and partner and direct motions reinforce each other Define how reseller marketing success is measured: set targets and KPIs for pipeline, reseller revenue, and campaign ROI, build the reporting, and use results to decide where to invest and what to change Report on partner-sourced pipeline and reseller revenue influence, with 30/60/90-day tracking on every activation Keep reseller partners informed through the CPN monthly broadcast and newsletter, and bring partner needs and results back into program planning Minimum qualifications Have owned marketing strategy for a partner or channel program, setting priorities and investment decisions rather than only executing against them Have built and run co-marketing programs with channel, reseller, or distribution partners, including partner-funded budgets (MDF, co-op, or similar) and ROI reporting Have sourced and managed agencies or contractors across multiple regions, including scoping work, managing budgets, and holding quality standards Have run marketing programs across multiple international markets Understand indirect sales motions, including how partners find, register, and close deals, and can write marketing that reaches partner sellers as well as end customers Can build joint plans and value propositions that articulate clear business outcomes for customers Have defined success measures for a partner or channel program and used the results to change investment decisions Are skilled at tracking program performance in a CRM or equivalent system, and can turn that data into clear recommendations Write clearly and precisely, and can hold partner-produced copy to brand and approval standards Build trusted relationships with partner marketing and sales teams, and can move priorities forward with partners you don't manage Can make and defend decisions with incomplete data, and know when to escalate Are highly organized and can run several partner plans at once without dropping quality Are comfortable building new processes from scratch, in an environment where the playbook is still being written Take ownership of outcomes and step in wherever the work needs you Care about the societal impacts of AI and are excited about enabling organizations to adopt AI responsibly Preferred qualifications Have 7+ years of marketing experience, with significant focus on partner marketing in B2B technology environments Have launched or scaled a partner program from its early stages, including tier design, benefits, and promotion criteria Have produced partner-led customer stories, including managing approvals and public announcement timelines Have experience with cloud marketplace reseller motions, such as private offers or co-sell programs Have localized marketing content and campaigns for multiple international markets Have established relationships with resellers, distributors, or systems integrators Have experience with partner relationship management tools and Salesforce partner data Understand enterprise AI use cases across industries and functions Have set standards for or mentored other marketers, formally or informally Have used Claude or other AI tools to scale their own marketing work The annual compensation range for this role is listed below. For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role. Annual Salary: $320,000 — $400,000 USD Logistics Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices. Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this. For roles performing work in California: We will consider for employment all qualified applicants, including those with arrest or conviction records or criminal histories, in a manner consistent with the requirements of applicable state and local laws, including the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the City of Los Angeles’ Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act. We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team. Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. You’ll help turn open-ended questions about model behavior into well-defined ML problems, build methods that address them, and establish how reliably those methods work. This role combines traditional machine learning, model evaluation, and real-time engineering. You’ll own classifiers throughout their lifecycle, including supervised fine-tuning, distillation, evaluation, deployment, and production inference. You’ll work closely with researchers to identify valuable problems and with software engineers to make promising approaches useful at scale. items.description: Ready to do the most impactful work of your career? At Coinbase , we are uncompromising on our mission to increase economic freedom. The bar is high, the environment is intense, and we like it that way. This isn't a place for complacency, it’s a place to be pushed past your perceived limits. If you're ready to build the future of finance alongside people who refuse to settle for "good enough," you belong here. Coinbase is a remote-first, but not remote-only company. Expect to get together quarterly for intense in-person working sessions called “surges.” Learn more about working at Coinbase . Coinbase is looking for an experienced SEC Reporting Manager to join our Financial Reporting organization. Reporting to the Director, SEC Reporting, this role will serve as a key owner of Coinbase’s external reporting process, including Forms 10-Q, 10-K, 8-K, earnings release support, and related audit and control activities. This role will coordinate with Controllership, Technical Accounting, FP&A, Investor Relations, Legal, Tax, and external auditors, while also helping drive improvements to our reporting infrastructure, Workiva processes, and disclosure operating model in a fast-moving public-company environment. What you’ll do: Own major portions of the end-to-end 10-Q / 10-K / 8-K production cycle, including calendar management, drafting coordination, review workflows, tie-outs, and final filing support. Lead complex disclosure areas, translating accounting, business, and operational changes into clear and decision-useful external reporting. Partner cross-functionally with Controllership, Technical Accounting, FP&A, Investor Relations, Legal, Tax, and external auditors to resolve judgmental issues and deliver timely, accurate filings. Drive structural improvements to SEC reporting, including Workiva, source-data flows, supporting templates, review controls, and process documentation. Support audit requests, quarterly board / audit committee materials, and other ad hoc analyses tied to external reporting. Coach and elevate junior team members through review, process discipline, and operating best practices. Required Skills and Experience: 9+ years of relevant experience in SEC reporting, external reporting, or public-company financial reporting, including recent hands-on ownership of 10-Q / 10-K processes. CPA or equivalent required. Strong knowledge of US GAAP, SEC disclosure requirements, SOX controls, and public-company reporting mechanics. Demonstrated experience owning complex disclosures, coordinating auditors, and managing cross-functional stakeholders under tight deadlines. Experience with Workiva (Wdesk), NetSuite, and spreadsheet-based analytical review in a controlled reporting environment. Strong written judgment, project management, and communication skills, with the ability to improve ambiguous or evolving processes. Utilizes generative AI responsibly, maintaining human oversight to deliver business-ready outputs and drive measurable improvements in workflow efficiency, cost, and quality. items.description: Synthesia is the world’s leading AI video platform for business, used by over 90% of the Fortune 100. Founded in 2017, the company is headquartered in London, with offices and teams across Europe and the US. As AI continues to shape the way we live and work, Synthesia develops products to enhance visual communication and enterprise skill development, helping people work better and stay at the center of successful organizations. Following our recent Series E funding round, where we raised $200 million, our valuation stands at $4 billion. Our total funding exceeds $530 million from premier investors including Accel, NVentures (Nvidia's VC arm), Kleiner Perkins, GV, and Evantic Capital, alongside the founders and operators of Stripe, Datadog, Miro, and Webflow. THE ROLE We’re hiring Solutions Engineers to build Synthesia’s pre-sales function in France and Southern EMEA. This is a founding role: you’ll be one of the first SEs, shaping the playbook, tooling and best practices as we scale, not following an established model. If you’re someone who is excited by building whilst scaling, we’d love to hear from you. As a Solutions Engineer at Synthesia, you will partner with Account Executives, Customer Success and Product Marketing to run discovery, deliver demos, scope POCs and design the technical solution for each deal. You will be a trusted advisor focused on the value customers get from Synthesia, and you’ll take what you learn in the field back to Product. This is an incredible opportunity to join us as we become a multi-product company for the first time, and continue to scale across France and Southern EMEA. WHAT YOU'LL DO - Co-plan and support discovery calls with your AE to understand customer requirements, technical environment, and business challenges. - Design and execute repeatable demo methodologies that prove Synthesia's business value quickly, whether the customer is deploying Studio at scale, building Roleplay Sessions for skill uplift, or integrating Interactive Avatars into their product. - Build and maintain strong working knowledge of Synthesia's platform capabilities, roadmap, and positioning across all product lines, so you can speak to the use cases that drive value - Deliver demonstrations that speak to customer problems and tell a credible story of why Synthesia is the right solution. - Identify technical objections and integration questions as they come up, working with your AE and the broader ecosystem to find a path forward. - Contribute your assessment of technical fit and opportunity risk to help your AE shape account and deal strategy. - Keep your deal team and manager informed on deal status, timeline, and technical dependencies. - Identify, build relationships with, and actively enable technical champions within customer organizations so they can advocate for Synthesia internally. - Provide technical guidance on platform capabilities, API and SDK integrations, security, compliance topics (SOC 2, GDPR, enterprise identity), and scalability for global deployments, troubleshooting issues and validating integrations with LMS, HCM, and content systems as they surface. - Partner with Enablement to complete certifications, stay current on new releases, and keep your demo and objection-handling skills sharp. WE’D LOVE TO HEAR FROM YOU IF YOU HAVE - 2+ years of pre-sales, solutions engineering, or customer-facing technical experience in a SaaS environment (or equivalent technical customer-facing experience). - Delivers a strong standard demo aligned to the discovery points and agenda set with the AE, with a solid grasp of core demo technique (e.g., Tell-Show-Tell). - Applies established solution designs and best practices to the customer's use case, working with core ecosystem functions (Product, Customer Success) as the deal requires. - Identifies and surfaces deal risk and next steps based on what the customer tells you, escalating clearly to your AE so it gets actioned. - Working knowledge of MEDDPICC and Command of the Message, and can articulate why Synthesia is a fit for the prospect. - Resourceful: knows how to find the right person or tool internally, and is building their own network across the GTM organization. - Comfortable with the technical fundamentals in at least one area (creation flows, APIs, integrations, security, compliance) and eager to build depth quickly. - Self-motivated and organized, able to manage a growing book of POCs, demos, and customer conversations while hitting deadlines. - Willing to travel for customer discovery and on-site demos as needed. - You like staying ahead of the AI-native learning and enablement space, so you can credibly discuss how customers are shifting from static methods to interactive practice and measurable skill development. - Strong written and spoken communication in English and French WE'D BE PARTICULARLY EXCITED IF - Like working in a fast pace environment - Can also speak Spanish and or Italian - Based in Paris or London so you can spend time in our offices. This is a hybrid role, with 2-3 days a week in the office. COMPENSATION We offer a competitive salary, equity and benefits. Your offer will reflect your experience, skills and the scope of the role.

items.title: Chief of Staff
items.description: WHO ARE WE? Cohere is the leading security-first enterprise AI company. We build cutting-edge foundation AI models and end-to-end products that are designed to solve real-world business problems. We’re training and deploying frontier models for enterprises who are building AI systems. We believe that our work is instrumental to the widespread adoption of AI and we are looking for folks that want to be part of that. We obsess over what we build. Each one of us is responsible for contributing to increasing the capabilities of our models and the value they drive for our customers. Cohere is a team of researchers, engineers, designers, and more, who are all passionate about their craft. We are a global technology company headquartered in Toronto with key offices in London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul. Join us! About the role We're hiring a Chief of Staff to keep Cohere's AI organization running at full speed. You'll report to and support the Chief AI Officer and work to bridge across all teams and functions at Cohere (including research, modelling, product, delivery, security, sales and operations). In any given quarter, the org ships new AI product releases and demos, customer pilots and scaled solutions, security updates, often across regions and time zones. Your job is to make sure the right work priorities win when everything feels urgent, that our plans turn into high-quality shipped work, and that our Chief AI Officer can focus on leading instead of firefighting. Much of this is operational: the planning calendar, the budget, the headcount plan, the weekly business reviews, the communication strategy (internal and external), the cross-functional handoffs. Your role is the operating rhythm of the org: meetings, priorities, plans, and the decisions that come out of them. You will be a member of an experienced, high-performing and supportive leadership team. What you'll own Own the operating rhythm and planning: annual and quarterly planning, goal-setting, and the weekly and monthly business reviews. Drive budget and headcount planning against the slate, and keep both honest as priorities shift mid-quarter. Keep major programs from colliding or stalling across research, modelling, product, delivery, and security. Be the person teams come to when it isn't clear who owns a decision, or how to navigate trade-offs. Be the connective tissue between the Chief AI Officer’s org and the rest of the company: cross-functional planning with product, engineering, security, and finance, so the org's commitments are realistic and its dependencies are visible. Own and lead special projects: Lead the things that don't fit neatly on any one team's plate: a reorg, a new partnership, a flagship research event, an org-wide planning week. Own them end to end. Who you are You have 12+ years of operating experience, with real time inside an AI/ML organization in a Chief of Staff, business operations, or senior program-operations seat. You know how to partner with teams shipping fast & often to high-stakes organizations, and you know how to change course with agility when needed. You understand how AI actually works—at the level of someone who's done it rather than managed it from a distance. You can talk credibly about how a model turns into a product, what data requirements demand from both research and engineering, and where delivery motions usually break. You're fluent in the numbers. Model performance metrics, data pipeline throughput, budget-to-impact. You don't have to run every program yourself. You do have to understand them well enough that the people who run them respect your judgment. You hold strategy and execution in the same hand. You can sit in a planning conversation with the Chief AI Officer in the morning and chase down a stuck deliverable in the afternoon. You thrive in a fast-paced environment, you handle ambiguity with curiosity and confidence, you stay calm when it's messy. You have a track record of bringing order to a fast, complex org without grinding it to a halt. You are an outstanding communicator and know how to wield soft power. Clear writing, straight talk, the ability to influence teams and individuals, and the executive presence to represent the Chief AI Officer in high-stakes conversations. FULL-TIME EMPLOYEES AT COHERE ENJOY THESE PERKS: - A weekly lunch stipend of $75/£75 or equivalent in your local currency for lunch. - Full health and dental benefits, including a separate budget for mental health. - RRSP matching, 401K, Pension Scheme. - 100% Parental Leave top-up for up to 6 months, for either parent. - Annual enrichment benefits: Arts & culture, fitness/wellness, quality time, and a workspace improvement credit. Education & learning stipend for conferences, courses, and coaching. - 6 weeks of paid vacation (30 working days!) - Budget for traveling to other offices if you are remote, plus an annual company offsite. HOW AND WHERE WE WORK: - Cohere is remote-friendly, but we also have offices in Toronto, London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul with more opening soon. - For those in the office: a daily lunch program, plenty of snacks, and regular community and social events. - For those not near an office: a co-working benefit so you can work alongside others in your city. - Everyone receives a $500 home office stipend to set up your workspace properly. If any of the above doesn’t line up exactly with your experience, we still encourage you to apply. We strive to create an inclusive work environment for all; we welcome applicants from all backgrounds and are committed to providing equal opportunities. Should you require any accommodations during the recruitment process, please submit an Accommodations Request Form https://docs.google.com/forms/d/12a6IrLdF3kI2nonKSr4tiFuz18rLQbaeYV-JM9L4o9Q/edit, and we will work together to meet your needs. We may use AI-enabled tools to screen and assess applicants against the criteria for this position. This helps our recruiters identify potentially qualified candidates, but it doesn't limit the applications our recruiters may review or consider. Beware of Scams: Cohere will never ask for payment or third-party services (e.g., CV writing) as part of our hiring process. All legitimate roles are listed on the Cohere careers page and LinkedIn only, with all communications from Cohere employees coming from an @cohere.com or @cw.cohere email alias. If jobs are viewed on other sites then please verify these through our official careers https://cohere.com/careers page.

This role blends strong product fluency, instructional design, and customer advisory. You will lead live workshops, deliver services, and design adoption interventions for audiences ranging from everyday business users to technical practitioners and executive leaders, helping customers understand not just what OpenAI’s products can do, but how to apply them effectively in real world workflows. As Kraken’s regulatory footprint and business complexity grow, this leader will own operational strategy, tooling, process design, and metrics—driving automation, AI adoption, workflow standardization, and vendor optimization. This leader will also be responsible for Legal’s financial, resourcing, and demand management foundations—ensuring the right work is done by the right resource at the right cost, with predictable outcomes as the organization scales. items.description: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the role Anthropic's Corporate Systems team runs the core collaboration platforms everyone here works in and builds the tooling and automation behind IT. That responsibility extends to the companies we acquire. Their people, devices, and systems have to come into Anthropic securely. You'll own the IT side of Anthropic's acquisitions: due diligence, integration planning, and integration. Before close, you'll assess a company's IT environment and give the deal team a clear read on risk and effort. You'll define the technical integration plan and its requirements: what moves, where it lands, in what order, what has to be ready on day one, and how each security gap gets closed. After close, you'll carry out that plan and bring the company's people, devices, and systems onto our stack. This is a hands-on engineering role. You'll hold admin, write code, build automation, run the cutovers yourself and bring in other teams when the work calls for their expertise or support. You'll lead this work for IT Engineering and partner with Security, Corporate Development, Legal, People, and Finance at every stage. M&A will be your primary focus and responsibility, but you'll be a full member of the Corporate Systems team; taking part in planning and reviews, using and contributing to the team’s tooling, and contributing to the roadmap. Early on, M&A will be most of your work, including using Claude to automate the repeatable parts of diligence and integration. As that automation matures, and when M&A load is light, you'll contribute to other parts of the team’s roadmap. Responsibilities Lead technical IT due diligence: assess a company's identity, applications, endpoints, and infrastructure, and brief the deal team on risk and effort before close Find the gaps between an acquired environment and Anthropic's security model, rate them, and build the mitigations into the integration plan Define the technical integration plan and its requirements: what moves, where it lands, in what order, and what has to be ready on day one Run the integration: take over administration, migrate people, devices, and data, and retire what's no longer needed, with support from other IT Engineering teams as required. Work with Business Technology, Client Platform, Corporate Network, IT Operations, and Security on their parts of each integration Keep Corporate Development, Legal, People, Finance, and the acquired company's team clear on where IT stands Build a repeatable IT M&A playbook and automate as much of it as possible with Claude When M&A work is light, contribute to core Corporate Systems projects You may be a good fit if you have 8+ years as a hands-on engineer in corporate IT. You have designed and shipped systems, carried out migrations or integrations yourself, and owned at least one area end-to-end, with experience supporting other areas: identity, applications, endpoints, or corporate infrastructure Experience administering enterprise identity and collaboration platforms such as Google Workspace, Slack, and an SSO provider, and working code in Python or similar against their SaaS APIs Working knowledge of endpoint management and security concepts, enough to lead diligence on an unfamiliar fleet A proven ability to understand an unfamiliar IT environment quickly and deliver a prioritized view of risk to non-specialists A record of leading technical projects that span several teams and run to a fixed date, while doing much of the engineering yourself Comfort working autonomously, with ambiguity and confidential information Clear communication with executives, legal and corporate development teams, and engineers at acquired companies Strong candidates may also have Prior M&A, carve-out, or company-to-company migration experience Experience across the full stack: endpoints, systems, applications, and infrastructure Hands-on experience managing a device fleet or running an MDM Experience working in or alongside a security team A record of building tooling that replaces manual IT work Using Claude or similar tools as a core part of how you work Representative projects Assess an acquired company's IT environment that nobody here has seen and produce a prioritized integration plan within days Design a way to size integration effort and risk for a company of any shape or size Automate bringing acquired people and devices onto Anthropic's identity and device management Write the IT risk memo for a live deal and present it to Corporate Development and Security leadership Deadline to apply: None. Applications will be received on a rolling basis. The annual compensation range for this role is listed below. For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role. Annual Salary: $325,000 — $360,000 USD Logistics Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices. Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this. For roles performing work in California: We will consider for employment all qualified applicants, including those with arrest or conviction records or criminal histories, in a manner consistent with the requirements of applicable state and local laws, including the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the City of Los Angeles’ Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act. We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team. Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings. How we're different We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills. The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences. Come work with us! Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. We are not satisfied with the limitations of centralized exchanges or the complexities of building decentralized order books. We aim to make trading easy, fast, and secure for everyone. How? By fusing the simplicity of CeFi with the power of DeFi. At the heart of the issue lies “liquidity”. Builders often grapple with a paradox; traders need liquidity, but liquidity demands traders. Our solution is simple as is bold – concentrate all liquidity into one order book. One order book that connects all the liquidity in the crypto space. Our ambition doesn't stop there. We're omnichain, championing chain abstraction. We envision seamless transactions, where the underlying blockchain is merely a detail. By concentrating liquidity, we aim to redefine the crypto landscape, making bridging and wrapped assets a thing of the past. We are Orderly, and we are here to revolutionize DeFi, democratizing access to financial opportunities and fostering a fair, equitable paradigm for all. A Glimpse into Your Future at Orderly Network What will you achieve? Manage social media and community operations targeting Chinese-speaking crypto audiences, growing Orderly’s brand awareness and engagement across relevant channels. Create engaging Chinese content around crypto market trends, Web3 ecosystem developments, and Orderly’s products and initiatives, while supporting English-language content and marketing activities when needed. Proactively connect with Chinese-speaking Web3 builders, KOLs, and ecosystem partners to build relationships and explore collaboration opportunities. Monitor crypto trends, community discussions, and content performance to identify opportunities and improve engagement. What challenges will you face? Staying on top of fast-moving crypto trends and turning them into relevant, engaging content for Chinese-speaking audiences. Building an active community and meaningful relationships with builders, KOLs, and ecosystem partners through consistent engagement and outreach. Managing content and community initiatives independently in a fast-paced, remote environment. About you: 2+ years of experience in social media, content creation, community management, or digital marketing. Strong Chinese writing and content creation skills, with the ability to communicate in English and support English-language content when needed. A good understanding of the crypto and Web3 ecosystem, particularly Chinese-speaking crypto communities. A proactive self-starter with strong ownership, good execution skills, and a willingness to learn and experiment. Fluent in written and spoken Mandarin Chinese and English. Experience in Web3, crypto, DeFi, or fintech. Experience managing social media accounts or growing online communities in the crypto space. Existing connections with Chinese-speaking Web3 builders, KOLs, or ecosystem partners. Familiarity with DEXs, perpetual trading, or DeFi infrastructure is a plus. Interested in Learning More? Our hiring process begins by meeting with our People Team, who help facilitate the process of placing you in your new role. You can expect to share your experience and ideas in online video interviews with our hiring team of management and potential new colleagues. If you have experience in developing trading systems or financial-related products is a plus. You can prepare for this interview by mentally organizing your strategies and opinions on topics such as Web3, cryptocurrency trading platforms, and your vision of how to succeed. Share this! Don’t be afraid of friends or co-workers stealing this job! We will find a place for you if you are unique and intelligent. Check out our External Referral Incentives Program as well.

You’ll lead and grow a Japan Applied AI team as Anthropic’s presence in the market continues to expand. Applied AI comprises Solutions Architects, Product Engineers, and Finetuning Engineers. Working alongside the existing Japan Applied AI leadership, you will scale processes and best practices for the region’s technical pre-sales engagements, help each team member achieve success, high productivity, and career growth, and represent Anthropic as a technical lead on some of its most important partnerships. In collaboration with the Sales, Product, and Engineering teams globally and locally, you’ll help enterprise partners incorporate leading-edge AI systems into their cutting-edge products and platforms. You will employ your excellent communication skills, in both Japanese and English, to explain and demonstrate complex solutions persuasively to technical and non-technical audiences alike. You will play a critical role in identifying opportunities to innovate and differentiate our AI systems, while maintaining our best-in-class safety standards. for your team, promoting growth and output Partner with the existing Japan Applied AI leadership to align on team structure, coverage, and best practices Work with a handful of the highest-value enterprise customers on their overall AI adoption strategies, focusing on pre-sales technical excellence including use case scoping, technical champion building, and POC execution Partner closely with Build and evolve core services for session lifecycle, streaming responses (e.g., gRPC/WebSockets), structured tool execution, memory/state, and policy/guardrails. Collaborate closely with product, quality, and application teams to prioritize the most impactful roadmap investments. You are: 3+ years of software engineering experience building production distributed systems or cloud‑native applications. BS/BA in Computer Science or related field, or equivalent practical experience. Product‑minded: you prioritize customer impact, clear SLAs/SLOs, and pragmatic iteration. Ownership‑driven with a positive, proactive attitude; comfortable leading projects or learning from battle‑tested engineers. Experience operating services on Kubernetes and at least one major cloud (e.g., GCP, AWS, or Azure). Familiarity with event/streaming systems (e.g., Pub/Sub, Kafka), caching (e.g., Redis), and data stores for low‑latency paths. Practical understanding of LLM/agents building blocks: tool/function calling, structured outputs, streaming, and model selection/routing. Strong observability and debugging skills: tracing (e.g., OpenTelemetry), metrics, dashboards, and production forensics. Background in one or more areas is a plus: policy/guardrails, multi‑tenant isolation, rate‑limiting, concurrency control, cost optimization. If you’re excited to shape how the world works, you’ll help build systems used daily across Microsoft Teams, Zoom, ServiceNow, Zendesk, GitHub, and many more. You'll be deeply embedded where people get things done. You'll ship agentic capabilities on an open, extensible stack, with the craft and care required for enterprise trust, as we bring Work AI to every employee, in every company. About the Role: The bottleneck in building reliable and useful AI systems isn’t writing code anymore. It’s knowing what good looks like, applying that knowledge and experience from production usage into building rigorous evals, and using those evals to guide continuous product self-improvement loops. As the Tech Lead Manager of AI Evaluations, you will lead a team of applied AI scientists and engineers and build the evaluation strategy and platform that helps Glean ship delightful and reliable AI experiences. You will make evaluation a continuous part of how we develop and operate models, harnesses, assistants, agents, and other AI products at Glean. You’ll guide the team in translating emerging AI/ML research into reliable evaluation systems, build scalable, efficient and reusable eval infrastructure and trusted quality signals, and work across R&D, product, and marketing teams to turn evaluation results into better products and customer outcomes. You will: Own the AI evaluation eng roadmap and technical direction end to end: from defining what success means and building the evaluation platform to integrating results into release and product decisions. Build scalable, reusable evaluation infrastructure for datasets, experiments, graders, trace capture and replay, result analysis, and dashboards. Make evaluations reproducible, versioned, cost-aware, and easy for product and engineering teams to use. Create and maintain representative evaluation sets from expert-curated examples, appropriately governed production signals, synthetic cases, and historical failures. Cover common workflows, edge cases, long-tail requests, adversarial inputs, and important user and domain slices; protect held-out acceptance sets from tuning leakage. Define a balanced quality measurement system for AI products, including correctness, groundedness, retrieval and context relevance, completeness, instruction following, citation quality, user preference, and task success. For agents, evaluate tool selection and arguments, multi-step trajectories, policy compliance, recovery, and final task state, not just the final response. Develop a fit-for-purpose mix of deterministic checks, model-based graders (including LLM-based autograders), and human evaluation. Establish clear rubrics; validate and calibrate automated judges against human judgments; and measure evaluator reliability and limitations so teams can trust and interpret scores. Integrate evaluation into development and operations: fast CI regression checks, broader pre-release suites, model and prompt comparisons, and sampled production evaluation. Build feedback loops from user feedback and production traces into new test cases, and use monitoring, canaries, and experiments to detect regressions and drift. Make quality tradeoffs measurable by connecting evaluation outcomes to latency, reliability, and cost. Help teams diagnose failures by slice and trace, prioritize improvements, and make evidence-based decisions about models, routing, prompts, and system changes. Build and lead a high-performing team of applied AI scientists and engineers; coach and develop team members. Partner closely with product, infrastructure, security, and application teams to align evaluation standards and deliver the highest-impact work. About you: 10+ years of experience in software engineering, ML infrastructure, data systems, or a related technical field. Experience must include building and operating production systems. 5+ years of engineering or applied AI team management experience, with a track record of technical leadership, developing engineers and scientists, and delivering cross-functional projects. Hands-on experience designing, building, or operating evaluation systems for LLM/GenAI products, including model-based evaluators or autograders; practical understanding of how to assess model, retrieval/RAG, assistant, or agent behavior. Strong judgment about measurement quality, including dataset representativeness, judge calibration, reproducibility, uncertainty, and the risk of optimizing to a narrow metric. Knowledge of public benchmarks across domains and capabilities is a plus. Product-minded and collaborative: able to translate ambiguous quality goals into clear measures, communicate findings to technical and non-technical audiences, and influence roadmaps across teams. items.location_text: San Francisco, CA | New York City, NY
items.description: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the role As a Data Engineer supporting Billing & Payments Engineering, you’ll join the Finance Data Engineering team and build the foundation for accurate, scalable billing and revenue data across Anthropic. You’ll work closely with Billing Engineering, Finance and Accounting, as well as Product and other partners, to turn billing and payments data into reliable metrics, reporting and insights. You’ll make sure teams have trustworthy data that scales with our growth, and you’ll lead your own projects to enable self-serve insights that help teams make data-driven decisions. Key responsibilities Partner with Billing Engineering, Finance and Accounting to understand their data and reporting needs, and translate them into technical requirements Design, build and maintain data models and pipelines in dbt that transform raw billing, usage and payments data into canonical datasets Own revenue data accuracy and reconciliation, making sure billing, usage and revenue data tie out across systems Define success metrics for billing systems, and build the data models and monitoring to track them Set data integrity standards and SLAs for timely, accurate delivery of billing and revenue data Share on-call and data operations responsibilities for Finance Data Engineering pipelines Build dashboards and self-serve data products that track core metrics and deliver insights across the company Promote best practices for dbt, data modeling and SQL Influence the Billing Engineering roadmap from a data systems perspective Build a thorough understanding of our data models and data architecture Minimum qualifications Experience as a Data Engineer, Analytics Engineer or in a similar role Experience with SQL and Python, and building multi-step data pipelines with tools like dbt Experience with workflow orchestration tools like Airflow, and version control with GitHub Familiarity with billing concepts such as invoicing, payments, credits, refunds and subscriptions, and experience working with data from billing systems Experience building dashboards and reporting in tools like Hex for multiple cross-functional teams Ability to prioritize and deliver practical solutions quickly Willingness to solve problems end to end, including work beyond the original scope Ability to define next steps and keep work moving when requirements are unclear Interest in Anthropic’s mission of building safe and beneficial AI Preferred qualifications 5+ years of experience as a Data Engineer, Analytics Engineer or in a similar role Experience partnering with billing, finance or accounting teams on revenue metrics and reconciliation Experience building an analytics or data engineering function from an early stage The annual compensation range for this role is listed below. For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role. Annual Salary: $320,000 — $405,000 USD Logistics Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices. Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this. For roles performing work in California: We will consider for employment all qualified applicants, including those with arrest or conviction records or criminal histories, in a manner consistent with the requirements of applicable state and local laws, including the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the City of Los Angeles’ Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act. We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team. Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings. How we're different We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills. The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences. Come work with us! Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Guidance on Candidates' AI Usage: Learn about our policy for using AI in our application process.
